name: Lazarus MR-1 'Mercy'
description:
A single-shot injector weapon disguised as a standard medical auto-injector, the kind carried by millions of people in GLMZ for medication delivery, allergy response, and BCI maintenance. The Mercy looks, weighs, and functions identically to a Lazarus-manufactured medical device — because it is a medical device, with one modification. The injection mechanism can be loaded with any liquid payload, and the delivery needle has been lengthened and reinforced to penetrate through light clothing and reach major blood vessels.

Lazarus officially produces the Mercy for clandestine medical operations — field medics who need to administer emergency treatment to unwilling or unconscious patients in dangerous environments. The weapon's medical camouflage means it passes screening checkpoints, security inspections, and even casual physical searches, because every third person in GLMZ carries an auto-injector for legitimate medical reasons. Hiding a weapon in the most common object in a city is a form of genius that borders on cruelty.

The Mercy's payload determines its lethality. Loaded with a sedative, it puts the target to sleep. Loaded with a paralytic, it immobilizes them. Loaded with potassium chloride, it induces cardiac arrest that is nearly impossible to distinguish from natural heart failure. The weapon is the delivery system; the intent lives in the chemistry.
legality: Classified as medical device (weaponized use prohibited)
specifications:
delivery method: Intramuscular injection
payload volume: 2ml
needle penetration: Through light clothing, 25mm depth
activation: Thumb-pressure trigger (identical to medical use)
weight: 35g
length: 120mm
form factor: Indistinguishable from standard Lazarus auto-injector
tactical_use: Covert chemical delivery at contact range. The operator approaches the target in any setting where close proximity is normal — crowded transit, medical examination, social gathering — and administers the injection through a brief physical contact. The gesture is identical to the accidental bump of a medical device in a pocket.
cultural_context: The Mercy has made auto-injectors frightening. In a city where millions of people carry medical devices that could be weapons, every accidental brush with a stranger's pocket becomes a potential assassination. Paranoid individuals have taken to carrying their auto-injectors in transparent cases to demonstrate they contain legitimate medication. The most intimate medical device has been weaponized, and trust in basic healthcare technology has been damaged.
known_users: Contract assassins specializing in undetectable kills
Medical professionals operating in hostile environments
story_hooks: A wave of cardiac arrests in a specific corporate department — seven deaths in three months, all attributed to stress and overwork. A junior medical examiner has noticed that each victim has a tiny puncture wound in the same location on the upper arm, consistent with an auto-injector deployment.

A Mercy loaded with an unknown agent has been recovered from a crime scene. Analysis reveals the payload is not a toxin — it's a gene therapy vector that rewrites specific neural pathways over 48 hours, leaving the target alive but fundamentally altered. Someone is using medical weapons to change who people are.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, clinical auto-injector the size of a thick marker — instantly recognizable as standard medical equipment. Cylindrical body with a slightly tapered needle cap at one end and a flat thumb-pad activation button at the other. The aesthetic is deliberately sterile and forgettable: the kind of device that vanishes into a jacket pocket without a second glance.
physical_description.dimensions: 120mm length, 18mm diameter barrel, 8mm needle cap protrusion
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light — 35g feels almost insubstantial in the palm, identical to legitimate medical injectors. The balance is perfect for one-handed operation, the weight distributed to feel natural during a 'casual' pocket bump.
physical_description.primary_material: Medical-grade polycarbonate body with reinforced injection chamber. Needle assembly is surgical stainless steel with tungsten-carbide tip.
physical_description.finish: High-gloss translucent polymer body in pale clinical white/off-white. The liquid payload chamber inside is visible through the semi-transparent casing — a deliberate design choice that makes it look MORE legitimate. Injection window shows graduated measurement marks like standard medical devices.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pharmaceutical white with muted gray accents. The Lazarus logo — a stylized phoenix rising — appears in subtle gray on the upper barrel. Small red indicator stripe on needle cap (standard medical convention).
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth polycarbonate with a slightly textured thumb-pad for activation — ergonomic, familiar, designed to feel like thousands of legitimate injectors in daily circulation.
distinctive_features: Transparent barrel reveals payload chamber and measurement graduations
Reinforced needle cap with subtle red safety indicator
Thumb-pressure activation button identical to commercial medical injectors
Graduated measurement window (2ml capacity clearly marked)
Subtle Lazarus phoenix logo in muted gray
Quick-release needle cartridge design for rapid payload swap
Micro-etched serial number only visible under magnification
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: LAZARUS BIOWORKS logo in 2mm gray serif lettering on upper barrel. Serial number micro-etched near the base of the needle cap. Lot code printed on the transparent chamber in faint gray ink. Product safety warnings in multiple languages wrap the lower barrel — identical to legitimate medical versions.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always pristine. The Mercy's effectiveness depends entirely on its medical authenticity. Field-worn examples are carefully maintained to preserve the illusion. Any corrosion, scuffs, or battle damage compromise its core advantage: invisibility in plain sight. Operators rotate fresh units regularly.
